observation: The canonical Stage1-28 run completed all 27 configured analytical stages on the stated ZL3b-x7 corpus.
method: Frozen multistage descriptive and confirmatory pipeline
controls: Stage-specific shuffles, block permutations, natural controls and metadata validation
result: A multiscale structural baseline and artifact set exists.
interpretation: Entry point for Phase I evidence, not one omnibus statistical result.
limitations: Different stages use different units and nulls; completion does not validate every interpretation.

observation: The best frozen width-2 natural inverse candidate reduced all four holdout structural metrics relative to the original stream.
method: Frozen structural-v2 inverse search followed by an 80/20 line holdout
controls: Doyle T2/T4/T8 calibration, natural-text width-2 audit, 30 deterministic token permutations
result: Holdout deltas were -0.000965 transition, -0.000797 relation, -0.044830 sequence-2 and -0.003044 sequence-3.
interpretation: The tested inverse did not restore the targeted structure.
limitations: Split and meaningful-effect threshold were not preregistered; tested family is narrow.
literature_relation: No equivalent direct literature test identified

observation: The inverse-transposition method recovered the known synthetic transform in top-3 for all three blinded cases and exactly for all three.
method: Blind synthetic known-transform recovery
controls: Doyle T2/T4/T8; metric correlation audit
result: True candidate was top-1 in 2/3 and top-3/exact in 3/3.
interpretation: The search can detect tested transforms under synthetic conditions.
limitations: Synthetic calibration is not evidence that Voynich is transposed.

observation: The frozen synthetic inverse-homophony gate failed and Voynich Phase B was not run.
method: Blind class and structural recovery with a prerequired gate
controls: Natural and transformed controls; development/validation split
result: Class recovery beat random in 9/9 but structural recovery passed only 3/9; gate FAIL; Phase B NOT_RUN_BY_DESIGN.
interpretation: The inverse method was not reliable enough for a Voynich claim.
limitations: This is a method failure, not evidence for or against homophony in Voynich.

observation: Voynich corrected adjacent-token MI was 0.090736 bits, 1.099% of capped token entropy, while edge-glyph corrected MI was 0.216302 bits, 6.271%.
method: Adjacent MI minus mean of 100 within-line shuffles
controls: Doyle, Longfellow, Astafiev and homophony transforms
result: Visible token identities carry weak average adjacent dependence while token-edge glyphs remain coupled.
interpretation: Ordinary-word interpretation of visible tokens is strained; structured boundaries remain possible.
limitations: Different transcription/sample from R&T; MI is not semantics.

observation: Position-independent global homophony reduced Doyle corrected token-order share toward but not to Voynich and opaque outputs made glyph-edge MI inapplicable.
method: H2/H4/H6/H8 uniform and frequency controls
controls: Untransformed Doyle and Voynich rows
result: Uniform H2-H8 share fell from 6.825% to 3.325% versus Voynich 1.099%.
interpretation: Simple homophony changes one target in the right direction but does not reproduce the joint fingerprint.
limitations: No glyph-edge comparison for opaque-token transforms; not all homophony systems tested.
literature_relation: Partial replication plus extension of prior cipher controls

observation: Six frequent Voynich glyphs were near-strict initial, medial or final specialists at the frozen thresholds.
method: Position frequencies with within-token permutation/FDR
controls: Doyle, Longfellow, Astafiev; positive controls
result: q initial 0.9912; N final 0.9856; e medial 0.9838; E medial 0.9765; i medial 0.9676; m final 0.9505.
interpretation: Token-internal glyph placement is strongly constrained.
limitations: Thresholded high-frequency subset; transcription glyphs need not be letters.
literature_relation: PARTIALLY_AGREES with longstanding positional descriptions; modern control extension

observation: Doyle H2/H4/H8 position-independent homophony generated zero high-frequency near-strict specialists.
method: Shared corrected seeded homophony generator
controls: Natural corpora and position-dependent/structured positive controls
result: All simple homophony controls had zero specialists versus six in Voynich.
interpretation: Simple position-independent homophony is insufficient for this positional property.
limitations: Does not test position-dependent homophony, structured token encoding or broad cipher classes.

observation: Voynich exact adjacent repetition exceeded a global null but not a line-preserving null.
method: Adjacent equality and permutation nulls
controls: Global and within-line shuffles; natural corpora
interpretation: Most exact-repeat enrichment is accounted for by line/local organization.
limitations: Null equivalence is property-specific; does not explain why line structure exists.
literature_relation: PARTIALLY_AGREES with Schinner and Timm-Schinner; stronger matched-null extension

observation: Voynich adjacent edit-distance<=1 rate remained enriched against global, line-preserving and frequency/length-matched controls.
method: Levenshtein-near adjacent pairs and matched nulls
controls: Global and within-line shuffles; frequency/length matching; natural corpora
result: Observed 0.058656; global 0.025631; line-null 0.050938; matched 0.034936.
interpretation: Local near-form organization is not reducible to vocabulary opportunity or line structure alone.
limitations: Edit distance is a formal similarity, not morphology or derivation.
literature_relation: PARTIALLY_AGREES with repetition/self-citation literature; methodological extension

observation: Insertions and deletions in adjacent near-repeat pairs concentrated at token beginnings.
method: Edit-operation position tabulation
controls: Substitution position and control corpora
result: Boundary-biased edit geometry was observed.
interpretation: Compatible with structured token formation, without identifying its cause.
limitations: Descriptive; pair dependence and multiple explanations remain.

observation: Increasing simple position-independent homophony monotonically lowered near-repetition below plaintext and away from Voynich.
method: Shared H2/H4/H8 glyph homophony control
controls: Doyle plaintext and Voynich
interpretation: Simple random homophony is incompatible with the observed near-repeat enrichment.
limitations: Narrow generator only; structured or position-dependent systems remain open.

observation: Voynich shared-EVA h2 was lower than the natural controls, but its magnitude changed with boundary representation.
method: Shannon plug-in h2 on explicit stream representations
controls: Natural corpora and glyph/token shuffles
result: Voynich continuous h2=2.7726 bits versus Doyle 3.5978; boundary-symbol 2.4458; within-token 2.5026.
interpretation: The visible glyph stream is unusually predictable under the stated estimands.
limitations: No finite-sample correction; sparse higher orders; representation-dependent.

observation: A held-out position-dependent first-order within-token model captured part, but not all, of token structure.
method: Frozen 60/20/20 contiguous block split and validation-only model selection
controls: Length/frequency, copy-mutate, structured-token and natural controls
result: POSITION_MARKOV_1 test cross entropy 2.360985 bits/glyph; generated near-repeat about 0.0234 versus TEST 0.0395.
interpretation: Constrained local formation is needed, with a separate sequence component still required.
limitations: Synthetic model class is limited and does not identify language, cipher or generator.

observation: A small adjacent form-similarity residual survives length matching.
method: Adjacent versus non-adjacent same-line matched pairs; frozen local transition model
controls: Length-pair matching, global and within-line shuffles, held-out preservation
result: Within-line adjacent near rate about 0.05855 versus matched 0.05663; classification FORM_DEPENDENCE_ONLY/PARTIAL.
interpretation: There is a weak local sequential component beyond raw vocabulary opportunity.
limitations: Small effect; no unique transition mechanism; rare transitions descriptive.

observation: Frozen repeated sequences replicate as frequency-relative patterns, but candidate higher-order dependence is sparse and position-sensitive.
method: Frozen-candidate FDR, block replication, conditional permutations and LOBO
controls: Frequency shuffle, Markov and block controls
result: 51/104 sequences were robust above frequency null; the n>=3 deep-dive produced two insufficient-support candidates and one position-dependent candidate, later classified NO_POSITIONAL_STRUCTURE under cross-block criteria.
interpretation: Sequence organization exists, but evidence for general higher-order rules is weak.
limitations: Frozen candidate selection, low counts and position sensitivity.
literature_relation: Methodologically distinct from most prior sequence work

observation: Same-line nonadjacent near-form similarity exceeded a same-page matched control, but shifted line-sized windows matched or exceeded the physical-line effect.
method: Length-matched pair rates, membership-destruction nulls and scale comparison
controls: Different-line same-page and different-page matches; shifted/fixed windows
result: 0.057824 versus 0.049905, delta +0.007939, bootstrap CI [0.004600,0.012813]; classification BROADER_LOCAL_REGIME.
interpretation: The supported scale is local and line-sized, not uniquely the physical line.
limitations: Scribal, layout, material and content causes are not distinguished.

observation: Local similarity and mixed drift/state topology were found, while metadata explained only part of the organization.
method: Lag curves, metadata-conditioned topology and frozen synthetic controls
controls: Stationary, smooth, discrete, mixed and natural controls; Task62 G-only
result: LOCAL_STRUCTURE CONFIRMED; TOPOLOGY MIXED_DRIFT_AND_STATES; METADATA PARTIALLY_METADATA_EXPLAINED.
interpretation: Voynich varies locally and heterogeneously, without identifying semantic topics or keys.
limitations: K=5 is descriptive/model-selected; topology labels are not causal states.

observation: After correcting the minimum-of-many shuffled-position null, distant recurrence did not exceed chance.
method: Nearest distant-window profile distance with calibrated shuffled positions
controls: Corrected multiple-opportunity null; both observed and null use the same minimum search
result: Lower distance means a closer, more recurrence-like match. Observed mean distance 0.046108 was not lower than null 0.002320; null-minus-observed was -0.043788.
interpretation: No evidence for recurrent discrete regimes from this test.
limitations: Absence of support under this statistic is not proof that regimes never recur.

observation: The Task64 discovery/replication split discrepancy reproduced independently.
method: Independent reproduction of frozen Task64 split
controls: Discovery versus replication partitions
result: Effect 0.030069436 in discovery versus 0.003132198 in replication; TRUE_REGIME_HETEROGENEITY.
interpretation: The split difference is a property of heterogeneous corpus regions, not a single reporting accident.
limitations: Does not identify the source of heterogeneity.

observation: Across the tested grid, constrained formation was required; homophony and stochastic output were disfavored, while several other components were not required.
method: Frozen multi-axis mechanism grid with held-out fingerprint scoring and ablations
controls: M0-M11, natural sources, validation/test split, component ablations
result: CONSTRAINED_FORMATION REQUIRED (delta 4.19); HOMOPHONY DISFAVORED; STOCHASTIC_OUTPUT DISFAVORED; memory, slow state, macro and generated boundaries NOT_REQUIRED.
interpretation: The tested fingerprint needs input-dependent constrained token formation more than added randomness.
limitations: Grid is finite; some held-out candidates inconclusive; below-threshold axes remain unexplained.

observation: Plaintext/input dependence was preserved in 33 of 36 strong or partial comparisons.
method: Frozen-input perturbation/dependence comparisons
controls: Shuffled and alternative natural inputs across candidate mechanisms
result: PLAINTEXT_DEPENDENCE_PRESERVED/SUPPORTED.
interpretation: Voynich-like synthetic compatibility does not require erasing the input signal.
limitations: Synthetic architectures only; not evidence that Voynich has plaintext.
literature_relation: No direct comparable prior test found

observation: In known-plaintext synthetic tests, M0/M1 and declared-codebook M2 recovered exactly, while constrained formation families were partial, ambiguous or fragile.
method: Frozen encode-decode, preimage, corruption and boundary-error batteries
controls: Three natural corpora, identity/bijection/homophony controls, shuffled input, error types and reset variants
result: M0/M1 reversible; M2 ambiguous but decodable; G/M9 intrinsically lossy; M10/M11 practically fragile.
interpretation: Reversibility, exact recovery, ambiguity and robustness are separate mechanism properties.
limitations: Synthetic known plaintext; decoder knowledge is declared and mechanism-specific.

observation: Boundary insertion/deletion and token split/merge can desynchronize tested decoders; resets can localize damage.
method: Single-error propagation and synchronization length
controls: Glyph errors, boundary errors, segmentation errors and reset policies
result: Boundary-count errors were the dominant desynchronizing class in affected mechanisms.
interpretation: Transcription and segmentation damage can dominate practical recoverability even when an encoder is mathematically reversible.
limitations: Tested mechanisms and error rates only; no Voynich error model inferred.

observation: Fingerprint similarity did not uniquely determine recoverability in the tested synthetic candidates.
method: Joint fingerprint coverage and recovery frontier
controls: Identity, bijection, homophony and constrained mechanisms on three corpora
result: Constrained candidates showed a compatibility/recovery trade-off and no control-level unique recovery.
interpretation: Voynich-like statistics alone cannot establish whether the manuscript is recoverable.
limitations: Finite candidate grid and approximate estimators; no inference of Voynich information loss.

observation: Task58's initial MI implementation was nondeterministic in low-order floating-point digits and was replaced by sorted-key accumulation.
method: Git/provenance audit and corrected rerun
controls: Byte/history comparison and determinism tests
result: Corrected artifacts at ba88b2de; qualitative conclusion unchanged.
interpretation: Only the corrected artifacts are current evidence.
limitations: Legacy manifest lacks dirty-status detail.

observation: Task59's original position-independent homophony generator leaked within-token position and was replaced by a seeded position-independent draw.
method: Implementation audit, regression tests and regenerated controls
controls: Position-dependent positive control and pool-spread tests
result: Original control implementation was invalid; corrected H2/H4/H8 results support the narrow negative finding.
interpretation: Use only corrected control artifacts from ba88b2de.
limitations: Manifest embeds a6904f0 while the completed corrected tree is ba88b2de.

observation: Task67's initial proxy outputs were replaced with measured encode-decode experiments.
method: Git tree provenance and measured rerun
controls: Artifact hash chain to frozen Task66 candidates
result: 553ef02 proxy scaffold is superseded; 0e8b3da measured artifacts are current.
interpretation: Only measured Task67 outputs support recoverability claims.
limitations: Top manifest lacks corpus SHA and dirty status.

observation: Task66's per-job seed and config hash are deterministically derivable in code but absent from frozen result rows.
method: Implementation and artifact provenance audit
controls: Config hashing and seed derivation inspection
result: Top-level design is preserved, but claimed row-level job identity is NOT_RECORDED.
interpretation: This lowers reproducibility confidence without invalidating stored measurements.
limitations: Exact job recreation requires reconstruction from code/call sites.

observation: No Phase I result conclusively selects H_L, H_C or H_G.
method: Claim-level synthesis across experiments and literature
controls: Natural, cipher, generator and shuffle controls
result: Broad alternatives remain PARTIALLY_DISTINGUISHABLE only.
interpretation: The current conclusion is structured symbolic organization plus constraints on narrow mechanisms.
limitations: No validated semantic oracle, decipherment or full three-class held-out comparison.
